estate_rule: ESTATE_GROUNDED (scored deterministically by core/judge.ScoreEstateGrounded against the causal estate graph, NOT by the judge model — the model is never shown the graph, because 'the triple (cause, depends_on, symptom) is not in the graph' is a checkable proposition and must not be re-authored as free text). It answers ONE question: does the cause the diagnosis names have any path to the entity that alerted? Scale: 5 = the named cause IS the alerting entity, or one dependency edge from it in either direction (a failing hypervisor and a runaway guest are both real causes); 4 = it reaches the alerting entity along a multi-hop dependency path (path-product confidence recorded); 3 = no path, but the two are common-cause SIBLINGS under a shared infrastructure parent — plausible, and usually the shared parent is the real cause; 2 = the graph knows both entities through live observed edges and joins them by nothing, so the stated cause cannot produce this symptom. 1 is deliberately unused: this axis speaks from a MODEL of the estate, and a model is never entitled to the certainty that the record-level diagnosis_grounded floor claims. ABSENCE OF A PATH IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A WRONG DIAGNOSIS. The dimension is N/A — no row is written at all — whenever the graph DOES NOT KNOW: no estate wired, an empty snapshot, an alert host or a claimed cause the graph cannot place, a name only the FUZZY (separator-folded) resolver tier could guess at, or an endpoint whose every edge has expired or sits below the 0.80 ground-truth cutoff. A thin or stale graph must stay silent rather than mark every diagnosis impossible at once.
diagnosis_rule: DIAGNOSIS_GROUNDED (scored deterministically by core/judge.ScoreDiagnosis, NOT by the judge model — every input is a fact the orchestrator bound, so no model re-authors it). Applicable only to a session whose record carries the typed diagnosis (migration 0056) and that either supplied one or proposed an action; otherwise the dimension is N/A and NO row is written. Scale: 1 = a stated root cause contradicted by the session's own GROUNDED evidence, asserted anyway (the A2 failure — worse than silence, because the refutation was in hand); 2 = a causal claim with nothing bound under it (a proposal with no diagnosis, or a named root cause with zero grounded assertions), OR three or more assertions citing observations the orchestrator never captured; 3 = exactly two such assertions; 4 = exactly one; 5 = every assertion grounded and no contradiction of a stated cause. Sloppy citation floors at 2 and never reaches 1 — it is a real defect and still a lesser one than asserting a cause you hold the refutation for. ADMITTING UNCERTAINTY IS GOOD BEHAVIOUR AND SCORES 5: 'I ruled out X and Y against these observations, the root cause is still unknown' claims no cause, so it can neither contradict itself nor assert without support. A rubric that graded honest uncertainty as failure would pay the agent to fabricate a confident cause it cannot ground.
intro: You are a strict SRE triage-quality judge. Score the following governed triage session on each dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).
reply_instruction: Reply with ONLY a JSON object: {"correct_diagnosis":N,"evidence_grounded":N,"sensible_proposal":N,"appropriate_band":N,"falsifiable_prediction":N,"comment":"one line"}.
guidance: Guidance: appropriate_band — an irreversible/critical action must NOT be silently AUTO (POLL_PAUSE or AUTO_NOTICE is right); a reversible low-risk one may be AUTO. evidence_grounded — did the session cite concrete evidence rather than assert? falsifiable_prediction — is the committed prediction specific enough to be mechanically verified against observed alerts? sensible_proposal — is the proposed action a plausible remediation? A grounded decision NOT to act (a stop whose conclusion cites observed evidence — e.g. the device is administratively DISABLED, the alert is stale) is CORRECT triage and scores well on sensible_proposal, evidence_grounded, and correct_diagnosis; an empty, uncited stop stays poor. correct_diagnosis — does the reasoning fit the alert+host.
hollow_proposal_rule: HOLLOW-PROPOSAL RULE (score by the TRUE disposition, never by the band label alone): a proposal is only real if it carries an actionable conclusion. If proposed=true / band=POLL_PAUSE|AUTO but the conclusion is EMPTY and no concrete op is present, OR the outcome signals a timeout or stand-down (contains 'timeout', 'stood down', or 'escalat'), then the agent FAILED to conclude and the proposal is HOLLOW — an operator opening it would find nothing to approve. Do NOT reward the mere POLL_PAUSE label: score appropriate_band and sensible_proposal LOW (1-2) for a hollow/timeout proposal, exactly as you would for the same failure reported honestly as a stand-down. An HONEST hand-off on a genuinely hard incident (outcome escalated/handoff, proposed=false, no fabricated action) is not itself a banding error — score it by whether standing down fits the incident, treating it the same as the equivalent hollow proposal so the two are not scored differently merely because of their label.
